findings.description: Round two's blocker 3 was fixed in the payload but not in the durable decision that justifies it, so the D1 trace is now false in exactly the way the round-two D5 trace was. session-log.md:11 records the Implementation decision as `**Use portable canonical guide links** `architectural: skill-workflow` -- Installed skill payloads cannot use relative links that escape the skill directory; a stable repository URL remains clickable in canonical and mirrored copies.` No stable repository URL exists anywhere in the branch any more: all six sources now carry the bare backticked path (`grep -rn state-artifacts skills/**/SKILL.md` returns the identical sentence at skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:17, skills/autopilot-roadmap/SKILL.md:16, skills/session-log/SKILL.md:15, skills/supervise/SKILL.md:17, skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:22, skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md:22), and the test constant was renamed accordingly from `GUIDE_LINK` to `GUIDE_REFERENCE = "docs/guides/state-artifacts.md"` (test_state_artifacts_guide.py:16). A repo-wide grep for `github.com/jankneumann/agentic-coding-tools/blob/main/docs/guides/state-artifacts` outside `reviews/` returns nothing. The decision's own title is also now inaccurate -- a bare backticked path is a reference, not a link, and nothing rendered is clickable. The consequence is worse than a stale sentence because docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md:12 carries the same text verbatim: that file is generated by `PhaseRecord.write_both()` step four, which skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355-372 documents as running 'last, and unconditionally' precisely because 'a session-log entry is the only thing that invalidates that index'. So the capability timeline -- the artifact every future skill-workflow change inherits its conventions from -- now publishes a rationale for a URL convention this branch deliberately abandoned, and hand-editing the generated file would be overwritten on the next session-log write.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the D1 decision text in openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/session-log.md:11 to state the convention actually landed -- a bare backticked repository-relative path, matching skills/coordination-bridge/SKILL.md:81, skills/vision/SKILL.md:116 and skills/session-log/SKILL.md:155 -- and retitle it away from 'links'. Then regenerate docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md through the phase-record writer rather than editing the generated entry by hand. session-log.md:36 ('relative links were replaced after the installer portability guard rejected them') should also name what replaced them.

findings.description: The three documents do now share the same eight-step algorithm in prose -- design.md:39-46, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:21-28 and skills/supervise/SKILL.md:138-153 all run Bootstrap locator, Roadmap definition, Roadmap execution state, Change execution state, Learning context, Phase history, Handoff context, Rebuild projections, with design.md's former seven-step form (the round-two nit that merged roadmap.yaml and checkpoint.json into one bullet, and cited 'steps 2-3' for handoff consistency) corrected to eight steps citing 'steps 2-4'. But the drift guard pins that agreement asymmetrically. `test_guide_pins_rehydration_order_and_conflict_rules` (lines 43-54) checks all eight markers against the guide, while `test_supervise_rehydration_matches_canonical_order` (lines 68-78) enumerates only seven: 'Rebuild projections' is absent from the tuple. Supervise's step 8 -- 'Derive queue and display state from the verified canonical records, never the reverse' -- is the one that carries the truth/projection invariant the whole change inherits from ri-07, and it can be deleted, or moved above step 7, with the suite still green. design.md's own eight-step listing is pinned by no test at all, so the artifact that defines the algorithm is the only one of the three free to drift.
findings.resolution: Add "Rebuild projections" to the `markers` tuple in test_supervise_rehydration_matches_canonical_order, and add an equivalent ordered-marker assertion over openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/design.md so all three carriers of the eight-step algorithm are pinned by the same mechanism.

findings.description: Round two's blocker 2 is genuinely fixed -- test_state_artifacts_guide.py:86-87 now calls `pytest.skip` when either mirror is absent, so a fresh checkout no longer raises FileNotFoundError from `.read_bytes()` -- but the plan artifacts have not absorbed what that means for enforcement. .gitignore:280-281 excludes `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, `git ls-files .agents/skills .claude/skills` returns nothing, and the only CI step that touches the payload is `bash install.sh --check` at .github/workflows/ci.yml:65, which skills/install.sh:40 documents as 'Validate the complete install payload and exit without syncing'. No CI job runs install.sh in sync mode. So in CI the six mirror cases always skip: the spec scenario 'Runtime skill mirrors are installed' (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:46-49) has no enforcing check anywhere except a developer machine that happens to have run install.sh -- which is what I confirmed locally, where md5sum shows skills/, .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ identical for supervise and session-log. change-context.md:12 still records the evidence unqualified as 'Focused GREEN: 15 passed' and 'Six parametrized cases; 12 byte comparisons when mirrors are installed' (the count itself is now correct, resolving the round-two arithmetic complaint), and design.md:57 states the mitigation as a manual 'run skills/install.sh and byte-compare' step. Nothing states that the CI outcome for this module is 9 passed / 6 skipped and that mirror parity is therefore an unenforced local convention.
findings.resolution: Either record the limitation explicitly -- in change-context.md:12 evidence and the design.md:57 risk mitigation, noting the CI result is 9 passed / 6 skipped and that mirror parity is a pre-push local gate -- or make it enforceable by having the test synthesize the install (run install.sh into a tmp_path target and byte-compare there), which removes the dependency on untracked checkout state.

findings.description: Round two's blocker 1 is resolved at the mechanism level: skills/pyproject.toml now lists `tests/state-artifacts` in testpaths (between `tests/codebase-atlas` and `expedite/scripts/tests`), the .github/workflows/ci.yml `test-infra-skills` job runs with `working-directory: skills` and executes `uv run pytest -v` with no path argument at line 70, and skills/tests/ci_coverage/test_ci_test_coverage.py `_covered()` unions `_testpaths()` with the ci.yml arguments, so `test_directory_is_reached_by_ci[tests/state-artifacts]` resolves. The file is also correctly inside scope -- work-packages.yaml lists skills/pyproject.toml in both locks.files:44 and scope.write_allow:61. What did not follow is the plan record. No task in tasks.md instructs the registration: 1.1 says only 'Add the structural contract test at skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py' and its Coverage field enumerates assertions; 3.2 was updated to run 'the CI test-coverage guard' but naming the verification is not the same as owning the edit. Neither does the change-context.md traceability matrix -- its 'Files Changed' column names docs/guides/state-artifacts.md, docs/guides/documentation.md, six SKILL.md files and the mirrors, but never skills/pyproject.toml, so the requirement 'the drift guard this change creates actually executes in CI' has no Req ID, no mapped test, and no evidence row. The same omission applies to docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md, which appears in the diff and in scope but only in the Design Decision Trace D5 row, not in the requirement matrix.
findings.resolution: Add a task under Phase 1 (or 3.1) that names registering skills/tests/state-artifacts in skills/pyproject.toml testpaths with the ci_coverage guard as its verification, and add the corresponding row plus Files Changed entries to the change-context.md traceability matrix for skills/pyproject.toml and docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md.

findings.description: The inserted sentence carries a stray definite article before the backticked path: 'Shared holder, writer, authority, fallback, and rehydration semantics live in the `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md`.' The convention this change correctly adopted writes the path without one -- skills/coordination-bridge/SKILL.md:81 ('`docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md`. The invariant is guarded by'), skills/vision/SKILL.md:116 ('Full rules: `docs/guides/worktree-management.md`'), and skills/session-log/SKILL.md:155 ('See `docs/guides/memory-conventions.md` for the full tag schema'). The identical sentence is duplicated verbatim across all six canonical sources and both runtime mirrors, so the wording is copied eighteen times; fixing it later costs an install.sh resync. Purely editorial: the test asserts on the substring `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md`, which is unaffected either way.
findings.resolution: Drop 'the' before the backticked path in all six canonical SKILL.md files and resync mirrors, if a mirror sync is being run for another reason anyway.

findings.description: Verified independently against the runtime rather than against the spec text: every inventory row resolves to a real writer. Roadmap checkpoint -> skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/checkpoint.py:39 sets `self.checkpoint_path = workspace / 'checkpoint.json'` inside CheckpointManager, matching the guide's `openspec/roadmaps/<roadmap-id>/checkpoint.json` holder. Phase record -> `PhaseRecord.write_both()` at skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355. Handoff document -> the local fallback under `openspec/changes/<change-id>/handoffs/` and the supervisor mirror `openspec/supervise/supervisor-record.json`, both named in the same row. The queue exclusion at line 15 ('The coordinator work queue is a derived projection, not a sixth authority class') points at docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md, which exists and is the same target skills/coordination-bridge/SKILL.md:81 cites, so the projection boundary has one destination rather than two. All six required columns are present in the header row and each of the five classes states missing/stale behavior with the first-run case carved out explicitly ('Absence is valid before the run starts', 'Absence is valid for a never-started roadmap').

Round-two blocker 1 verified resolved end to end by reading both mechanisms, not just the diff. `tests/state-artifacts` is now a testpaths entry; .github/workflows/ci.yml declares `defaults.run.working-directory: skills` for the `test-infra-skills` job (lines 40-44) and its 'Run infrastructure skill tests' step is a bare `uv run pytest -v`, which is exactly the invocation the pyproject comment on the tests/setup-coordinator entry says must be used to make a testpaths entry load-bearing ('Verify this entry by collecting with NO path argument -- naming the directory bypasses testpaths'). On the guard side, skills/tests/ci_coverage/test_ci_test_coverage.py `_test_dirs()` rglobs test_*.py and yields the parent relative to skills/ ('tests/state-artifacts'), `_testpaths()` strips trailing slashes off the same strings, and `_covered()` unions the two, so `test_directory_is_reached_by_ci` returns on the direct hit without needing the ancestor fallback. The new module imports only pathlib and pytest, so it is safe in the shared session the pyproject NOTE warns about for skills that import siblings by flat module name.

The mirror check is now safe in the absence of the ignored runtime trees, and the guard is placed correctly. `test_changed_skill_mirrors_are_byte_identical` reads the canonical bytes first, then tests `agents.exists()` and `claude.exists()` and skips with a message that names the reason ('runtime mirrors are installed artifacts, not tracked checkout inputs') before either `.read_bytes()` on a mirror path can raise. Both paths are checked, so a half-installed tree skips rather than erroring on one and asserting on the other. ROOT resolution is correct for the new depth: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]` walks state-artifacts -> tests -> skills -> repo root, which is what every path in the module depends on. RED validity is unaffected by the change: with the guide and links absent the module still yields 9 failed / 6 passed as validation/red-state-artifacts.md:4 records -- test 1 and test 2 fail on the missing guide, the six link cases fail, the supervise-order case fails, and the six mirror cases pass on the author's machine -- which totals the 15 collected tests exactly.

Supervise is the one of the six skills where prose was genuinely replaced rather than only appended (16 deletions against 30 insertions; the other five are pure +4 additions of the pointer block, which is correct because their remaining loop-state references are phase-specific mutation commands the plan explicitly preserves). The replacement keeps bootstrap and verification separated at both ends: step 1 constrains the locator -- 'This selects the newer valid handoff or mirror only as a locator' -- and step 7 closes it -- 'canonical state wins even when the handoff is newer'. Step 3 carries the first-run carve-out operationally ('Absence is valid only for a never-started roadmap; a resume claim without it is degraded and stops automatic advancement') and step 4 forbids reconstruction ('Never reconstruct a missing or invalid loop state from the supervisor record'), which is the ri-09 failure proposal.md:7 cites. Nothing operational was lost in the compression: the `try_handoff_read(limit=1, supervisor_only=true)` call, the cycle_state.py rehydrate command, the `Degraded: handoff` report and the cycle-ledger.json read all survive inside the new step structure. The guide reference itself now matches repository convention -- a bare backticked repo-relative path, which is payload-safe without depending on a hostname and is not a relative link that would trip skills/shared/validate_install_manifest.py.

Package DAG, scope and validation weight all check out for a documentation-only surface. One package, `depends_on: []` (line 38), so there is no cycle, no cross-package overlap and no scheduler ordering question -- design.md:49-50 states the reason (concurrent edits to six shared SKILL.md files carrying an identical block would conflict for no throughput gain). All ten `locks.files` entries reappear in `scope.write_allow`, so nothing is locked-but-unwritable or writable-but-unlocked. `write_allow` enumerates exact paths, using globs only where a directory is the genuine unit (`skills/tests/state-artifacts/**`, the change directory), honouring the design.md:50 prohibition on repository-wide write globs; `deny` blocks agent-coordinator/src/**, agent-coordinator/database/** and apps/**, consistent with the proposal's Non-Goals. The `context_impact.surfaces` list now declares `decisions` alongside `documentation` and `semantic_code`, which is the validator-required counterpart to docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md being in scope. Verification is two commands producing exactly the two result_keys `outputs.result_keys` declares, at tier B, with security/deploy/browser recorded N/A at design.md:66 -- proportionate given the product diff is Markdown plus one dependency-free test module.

No new authentication, authorization, input-validation, deserialization or secret-handling surface is introduced, and the contracts declaration says so accurately rather than by omission: 'No OpenAPI, database, event, or generated-type contract applies.' Confirmed against the change's own commit range (e8019bfb~1..HEAD), which touches only Markdown, JSON/YAML plan artifacts, one TOML testpaths line and one test module -- no agent-coordinator source, no migration, no HTTP surface. The one new executable file reads files and compares strings; it imports pathlib and pytest and nothing else. Skipping the security-review phase is the correct call here rather than a deferred obligation.

Two round-two items verified fixed in this file and its downstream trace. D5 now permits the generated index explicitly -- 'The generated `docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md` index remains an allowed derived projection and is regenerated by the standard phase-record writer' -- which removes the contradiction with the branch diff, and change-context.md:22 was updated in step ('D5 - No hand-authored ADR | Generated decision index is allowlisted as a derived projection'), so the design decision, the trace row and the work-package scope now agree. The scope reconciliation at plan-findings.md:37 keeps the granularity right by naming the single derived file rather than opening docs/decisions/**. Separately, the guide's Writer ordering paragraph (docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:40) now names the fourth step -- 'and then regenerates the derived capability decision index' -- which I confirmed against the runtime docstring at skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:356-372: 'Best-effort 4-step persistence: markdown -> sanitize -> coordinator -> regenerate the decision index', with step four documented as running 'last, and unconditionally'. Guide and implementation now describe the same four steps in the same order, which is what the guide's own closing rule at line 44 demands.
